extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary criticism; editors, librarians, and collectors evaluating short-story collections and individual short stories
extracted.subtask_description: Critical evaluation of short stories and short-story collections (circa 1917), identifying qualities that mark excellence in characterization, imagination, authenticity, form-suitability, psychological depth, and stylistic power. Uses judgments and exemplars from the Yearbook's Roll of Honor and 'Best Books of Short Stories' critical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories of special excellence (asterisk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: Stories of special excellence are indicated by an asterisk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor marks certain entries with an asterisk to denote 'special excellence' among the listed stories; this is an explicit selection/flagging mechanism for outstanding works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated inclusion in the Rolls of Honor
rubrics_metrics.description: The index figures 1, 2, and 3 prefixed to the name of the author indicate that his work has been included in the Rolls of Honor for the 1914, 1915, and 1916 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior inclusion in earlier Rolls is used as an informational metric indicating sustained recognition; repeated appearance signals an author of established merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homely humanity of characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The homely humanity of his characterization’ (praise of Aumonier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warm, realistic, empathetic portrayals of ordinary people — characters whose humanity and domestic truth make them memorable and believable — are a mark of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rich imaginative talent / imaginative world-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should display 'rich imaginative talent' and the creation of a 'new imaginative world' or 'beauty of imaginative life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality of imagination and the ability to create an internally convincing imaginative world (whether animistic magic, local color, or psychological landscape) are central evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Didactic intention subordinate to artistry
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘He has a certain didactic intention in these stories, he has kept it entirely subordinate to the artistry of his exposition.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral or didactic aims are acceptable but should not overwhelm the artistic qualities; the story's craft and exposition should come first, with any moral point kept subordinate and unobtrusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability of characters (few well-drawn characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘It is the few characters which he has added to English fiction that we remember after his somewhat obvious moral has been conveyed.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A small cast of vividly rendered characters that linger in the reader's memory is preferable to a larger, less-drawn ensemble; strong characterization can redeem or balance an obvious moral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of depiction / indigenous flavor
rubrics_metrics.description: Praises such as 'the racy humor of these narratives is thoroughly indigenous' and that the studies 'approach far more closely to the heart' of their people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic local color, indigenous speech, and cultural specificity — even if written from outside the community — enhance credibility and depth; avoid condescension or inauthentic caricature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic quality / lyrical prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used include 'poetic study', 'prose poem', and noting that an author 'conveyed more poetry into' a short-story volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lyrical, poetic language and a sustained tonal beauty in prose are valued; stories that function as poetic studies or prose-poems can be judged especially worthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological revelation and mordant self-analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Praises like 'the psychological revelation of the mind... is complete' and 'bitter irony and mordant self-analysis' characterize some collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deep psychological insight, frank self-analysis, and the courage to dissect character and social mentality (even when realism is 'appalling') are important virtues in serious short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with an author's best previous work
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In these fifteen short stories Mr. Blackwood has adequately maintained the quality of his best previous animistic work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A collection should either maintain or exceed the author's established standard; consistency of quality across an author's oeuvre is a positive indicator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and variety (tone and genre)
rubrics_metrics.description: Noted range 'from tragedy to social comedy' within a collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Versatility — the capacity to handle multiple tones, genres, or moods within a single volume — is a virtue, demonstrating breadth of talent and the collection's overall interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form suitability: short story as author's true medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertion that 'the short story is her true literary medium.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the short-story form best serves the author's gifts; some talents reveal themselves more fully in short fiction than in the novel or other forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtlety and restraint of irony
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A subtle irony pervades them, but it is so definitely concealed that its insistence is never evident.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irony should be deft and integrated rather than obtrusive; the most effective irony is pervasive but tactfully restrained so it enriches rather than dominates the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid dramatic power
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise for works having 'vivid dramatic power' in portrayal and narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should often demonstrate dramatic intensity and vivid scenes that convey action, character conflict, or emotional force with clarity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative merit within literary tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons such as 'has the same flavor...that one enjoys in the novels of William De Morgan' or 'serves the same altar of beauty...that John Keats served.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placing an author within or relative to literary predecessors (comparative judgment) is used to signal stylistic lineage, strengths, and the kind of reader response the work may elicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strength of individual stories within a collection
rubrics_metrics.description: 'There is no story in this volume which would not have made the reputation of a new writer' and noting multiple stories worthy of high distinction (three stars).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both the collection as a whole and the individual stories; a volume whose constituent pieces are each strong enough to stand alone is particularly prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability as an introduction to an author
rubrics_metrics.description: 'I can hardly find a better introduction than "Day and Night Stories" to the beauty of Mr. Blackwood's imaginative life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a collection functions well as an entry point to an author — clarity, representative quality, and accessibility make a volume a good 'introduction'.
